title: Tenant-facing brief: model pin rollback and recovery choices (draft)
body:
Summary (TL;DR):

On 2029-10-03 03:12 UTC we observed a service degradation that affected deterministic outputs for a subset (~3%) of tenants using pinned model versions on Dedicated and Private deployments. Root cause (prelim): a model-version pin rollback automation introduced a timing race with the private control plane deployment path. In a narrow window some requests were routed to a temporarily inconsistent model variant (mismatch between model binary and caching metadata), which produced duplicate or truncated structured outputs and, in a few cases, token-order changes for streaming responses.

Impact:
- Tenant-visible symptom: duplicated or partially truncated streamed responses, occasional out-of-order tokens for structured tool-calling responses.
- Fraction of traffic affected: approximately 3% of requests across Dedicated + Private, concentrated in East US and EU regions where rollback coordination was in flight.
- Customer-visible effects: mild application errors for 2% of impacted customers (edge-case parsers), increased error rates for structured outputs. No customer data was exfiltrated.

Staff actions taken (high-level):
- 03:18 UTC: auto-rollback was paused; routing policy reverted to last known-good variant.
- 03:30 UTC: target tenants routed to stable replica; KV cache warmup forced for affected model pool.
- 04:10 UTC: monitoring thresholds returned to baseline; customers with high error rates identified and grouped for follow-up.

Suggested short status page update (one-line for status.redwood.ai):

"Partial disruption for pinned model versions in East US/EU; engineering applied a targeted rollback and results are stabilizing. If you see duplicated or truncated streamed responses, check your integration settings and contact support."

Suggested detailed customer postmortem (plain language):

What happened
A background rollback process that ensures tenants run a pinned model version encountered a coordination race with the private control plane in two regions. During a brief window some requests were served by a model binary whose caching metadata (KV/per-request index) was not yet aligned. That mismatch produced a small number of duplicated or truncated streamed responses and, rarely, token-order differences in multi-part structured outputs.

Why this matters to you
Most applications will not be affected. If your app parses streaming structured outputs strictly (e.g., expects a single top-level JSON event per stream chunk), you may have seen parse errors, duplicate events, or truncated objects. We take that seriously and want to make it easy for you to recover.

What we did about it
- Immediately paused the rollback automation and reverted routing to the stable model variant.
- Forced cache re-warm on the affected model pools to ensure consistent KV state.
- Deployed an automation fix that adds a preflight handshake between control plane and model runtime to guarantee cache/version alignment before traffic is switched.

What you can do (Customer choices)
Option A: Accept the automatic mitigation (recommended)
- No action needed. We routed you back to the stable variant and warmed caches. If you continue to see issues, open a support ticket with "INC-4321" in the subject and we will prioritize a replay.

Option B: Request a targeted replay of affected requests
- We can run a tenant-scoped replay for eligible requests from the incident window. Replays are best-effort and may not be identical if your workload used non-idempotent side effects (external calls triggered by model outputs). To request a replay, reply to your support ticket and include the last request id/time window (we will provide an example).

Option C: If you require an immediate configurable mitigation (enterprise-only)
- We can provision a temporary routing pin to a dedicated stable model replica with an enforced cache-lock handshake. This requires an ops change and may incur a short maintenance window. Contact your TAM.

Timeline (UTC, preliminary)
- 2029-10-03 03:12: observed increased parse errors from customers in EU-East and US-East.
- 2029-10-03 03:15: alerted; active investigation begins (SRE + Serving Runtime + Private Control Plane).
- 2029-10-03 03:18: identified rollback automation as common factor; paused automation.
- 2029-10-03 03:30: routed affected tenants back to stable variant; kicked cache re-warm.
- 2029-10-03 04:10: error rates returned to baseline; monitoring shows resumed normal streaming token ordering.
- 2029-10-03 05:00: customer grouping and follow-up plan started; internal postmortem task created (JIRA-INC-4321).

Follow-up and prevention
- Short-term: automation change to add preflight handshake and additional gating metrics (deploying 2029-10-04).
- Medium-term: extend canary gating to include active kv-cache alignment checks and add a model-variant readiness probe that validates sample inference outputs before routing traffic. (Q4 initiative under serving-runtime).
- Customer support: offer replays and tenant-scoped verification; send tailored follow-ups to impacted accounts.

Sample customer communication (email snippet)

Subject: Update: brief disruption affecting pinned model versions (INC-4321)

Hi <customer-contact>,
We wanted to let you know about a brief disruption on 2029-10-03 that affected a subset of customers using pinned model versions. A background rollback coordination issue caused a small percentage of streamed responses to be duplicated or truncated. We have already reverted the routing, warmed caches, and deployed a fix to prevent the same coordination race.

If you saw duplicate or truncated outputs and would like us to replay the requests from the impacted window, reply to this email and we will prioritize. For urgent help, open a support ticket with "INC-4321" in the subject.

Thanks for your patience — Sophie (Customer Reliability)

Internal notes / TODOs
- Confirm exact list of affected tenant IDs with infra logs (Mateo).
- Draft tailored messages for top-10 impacted customers (Priya).
- Add postmortem write-up to Confluence with root cause trace and code-links (Jamal).
- Follow-up engineering checklist: verify new preflight handshake metrics in staging, add unit test for model-run readiness probe.

Open questions
- Are there any downstream integrations that would have externally observable side-effects that make replay unsafe? (ask Solutions Eng).
- Confirm whether any private on-prem customers saw differing behavior due to air-gapped control plane latencies.

Notes to self (working doc style)
- Keep the status page short and move technical detail to the postmortem so enterprise customers have something to read.
- Avoid language that over-promises identical replays — explicitly call out non-idempotent behavior caveat.
- Link to Jira and Slack thread in the final email.

Attachments we will include in final release
- Incident timeline CSV + top-50 sample request ids (redacted)
- Root cause trace snapshots from serving runtime (engineer-runbook)
- Replay request form for customers (simple checklist)

Draft owner: Sophie Chen (customer-reliability). Please add comments inline and flag any wording that might raise legal/compliance questions before we send to external customers.
